title: Specific Heat Capacity (c) — Definition & Key Values
topicTitle: Measurement of specific heat capacity of solids and liquids
notes: **Definition:** Setting m = 1 and Δθ = 1 gives c = H, so specific heat capacity is the heat energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by 1°C (or 1 K)
**Water:** c = 1 cal/g°C (CGS) = 4200 J/kg·K (SI) — unusually high, which is why water resists temperature change and is used as a coolant
